references.title: Wheeler Marsh: inundation, depth and tide-gauge methods
references.description: Extends the Wheeler study with HH/HV sigma-zero thresholds, a DEM and calibrated synthetic tide gauges. P02 now adapts the joint threshold rule after native conversion, but does not reproduce the filtering, depth, volume or published accuracy.

references.title: Wheeler Marsh: USGS NISAR validation site

references.title: Bridgeport tide gauge: context for the satellite dates
references.description: Check measured water levels at each acquisition time, rather than predictions alone. Levels use a stated vertical datum and do not measure water depth in each marsh pixel; local tidal lag and ponding still matter.

reports.title: Wheeler Marsh · source data, tides and earlier method

question: How often do marsh cells meet a paper-inspired HH/HV inundation rule on six observed dates?
method: The integrated method multiplies native linear HH and HV power by the delivered gamma-to-sigma factor before averaging to 20 m. A candidate must satisfy HH sigma-zero < −14 dB AND HV sigma-zero < −23 dB. The bundled independent wetland polygons define the marsh domain and named zones. Frequency counts observations; no reference rectangle is needed.
expected: The integrated previous run mapped 0.1228–0.6784 km² per date. Its nearby-gauge Spearman association was 0.829, versus 0.314 for the previous HH-only method. On 3 September, candidates covered 0.6784 km². These six-date associations are descriptive, not classification accuracy.
interpret: Start with observed water-candidate frequency on a fixed 0–1 scale. One sixth means one of six usable observations, not one sixth of all elapsed time. Explore time shows the six measured snapshots. Named-zone plots compare the supplied habitat zones; their labels are independent inventory information.
limits: The publications use historical PALSAR scenes, different dates, filtering and field/tide modelling. This is a transfer of their HH/HV rule to new NISAR data, not a recreation of the published pixels. The Bridgeport gauge is nearby rather than an in-marsh flood label; tidal lag and vegetation matter. Do not infer depth, volume or continuous hydroperiod. The 9 October gauge record was provisional in the archived receipt; nearby-gauge levels are not marsh water depth. The source report retains tide-screening dates, timing and weather context.

visual_comparison_note: This is a method-transfer comparison, not a same-date map match. The historical study estimates inundation and depth from PALSAR plus terrain and field evidence; our NISAR result reports water-candidate frequency. The study’s accuracy cannot be assigned to this app.

evidence.label: Method adaptation with tide context
evidence.description: A historical HH/HV wetland rule transferred to six NISAR observations, with descriptive nearby-gauge association; no pixel-level inundation accuracy is established.
evidence.transfer_validation: Not established on an independently held-out event or region.

comparison_review.conclusion: A historical HH/HV wetland rule transferred to six NISAR observations, with descriptive nearby-gauge association; no pixel-level inundation accuracy is established.
agrees: The nominal HH/HV sigma-zero thresholds follow the historical marsh method.
The archived six-date candidate-area series is more strongly associated with the nearby tide gauge than the earlier HH-only series.
differs: The papers and reference panels use historical PALSAR dates, field measurements, filtering and tide/DEM modelling; our dates are August–October 2026 NISAR.
A nearby Bridgeport gauge supplies context rather than contemporaneous labels for each marsh cell.
unverified: Spearman 0.829 for six observations is descriptive association, not accuracy or causation; no independent test set is supplied.
Historical published accuracy, depth and volume results do not transfer to this run.
comparison_review.next_check: Contemporaneous in-marsh water-level/inundation measurements, independently sampled labels and more tide states.
